digest: finding-003 is real for the string values "cancelled" and "timeout" (C1 says exactly three), but the boolean cancelled flags fall outside C1's stated scope, so the claim is narrowed.

evidence.relevance: Accepts two strings beyond the exact C1 set (aborted, AbortError, ABORT_ERR) in the error/reason candidates.

evidence.relevance: Code comment states the intended exactness, so the extra strings are drift from the author's own intent.
C1 explicitly limits the exact three-value rule to error and reason strings and says other provider errors must not be promoted.

counterEvidence.relevance: C1 scope is error and reason strings. It does not explicitly address non-string boolean flags, so the cancelled===true branch is not clearly a violation of the quoted rule.
Boolean flag check; outside the string-value rule as written in C1, so it should not be the basis of the finding.

finalClaim: isWorkflowReturnedCancellation treats the strings "cancelled" and "timeout" (in error or reason fields, including details) as cancellation, although C1 allows exactly aborted, AbortError, and ABORT_ERR. This violates C1's explicit rule against promoting other provider errors to cancellation. The cancelled boolean flags are not clearly covered by C1 and should not be counted as this violation.
recommendedAction: Remove "cancelled" and "timeout" from the string list at src/workflow-cancellation.ts:20 so only aborted, AbortError, and ABORT_ERR remain. Decide separately whether the cancelled boolean flags are intended and, if they are, document them in SPEC.md. Add a unit test covering "cancelled" and "timeout" strings returning false. The repository has no test files at all (no *.test.* or *.spec.* matches), so Q1 coverage for C1 is absent.
